messages:
anya: FYI I kicked off a quick bring-up for mirage-v1 (multilang) against wiki-holdout + lang-holdouts. saw an odd cross-lingual pattern: overall recall@10 down ~2.1% but non-en short queries (<=6 tokens) suffer much more. dropping snapshot + plan.
ben: ouch. can you paste the raw numbers and exact eval flags?
anya: paste below:
```
baseline: beacon-v2 fp16 (all)   recall@10 = 0.648  recall@1 = 0.402
mirage-v1 fp16 (all)             recall@10 = 0.627  recall@1 = 0.375  (-0.021)
mirage-v1 int8 per-channel      recall@10 = 0.621  recall@1 = 0.368  (-0.027)
NDCG@10 baseline 0.715 -> mirage 0.694
mean pos cosine: baseline 0.79 -> mirage 0.74

breakdown (shortseq <=6):
  en: baseline r@10 0.642 -> mirage 0.621 (-0.021)
  es: baseline r@10 0.635 -> mirage 0.588 (-0.047)
  ja: baseline r@10 0.619 -> mirage 0.556 (-0.063)
```
flags: `--model mirage-v1 --holdout wiki,lang-holdouts --k 10 --norm cosine --seed 314` vectors saved L2-normalized in artifacts. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/mirage/v1/multilang-smoke/
anya: also found tokenization shift: avg subtokens per short query increased (mirage tokenizer added more splits for CJK + emoji handling). may explain ja/zh hit.
luca: important. did you check topk overlap / id-flips per language?
anya: top1 overlap shortseq: en 0.81->0.74, es 0.79->0.62, ja 0.78->0.51. top10 overlap shortseq: en 0.95->0.90, es 0.94->0.84, ja 0.93->0.77. so big id-flip signal for non-en.
maya: curious if this is a norm/center shift or real semantic degradation. emb norm stats?
anya: yes: mean raw L2 norm (pre-renorm) for shortseq: baseline 8.9 -> mirage 7.1 for ja; en drop smaller. histograms in artifacts. positives' cosine mean shifts left ~0.09 for ja shortseq.
ben: quant effect looks small but non-negligible. run per-channel int8 calibration sweep anyway. also test per-tensor for comparison.
luca: also test HNSW efSearch/efConstruction sensitivity. smaller efSearch can worsen short-query top1 ties for low-norm vectors. try efSearch=128/256.
anya: quick mitigation experiments run: (A) global mean-centering + renorm -> mirage fp16 r@10 all 0.637, ja shortseq 0.582 (partial recovery) (B) PCA-whiten k=64 index-time -> r@10 all 0.639, ja shortseq 0.587 (C) tokenization-backfill: rerun mirage tokenizer with legacy hf-tokenizer for ja on a small sample -> r@10 ja shortseq 0.603 (big win). artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/mirage/v1/quick-mitigations/
ben: tokenization experiment is telling. if legacy tokenizer recovers JA a lot, then model/input pipeline mismatch likely. can you produce a small CSV of impacted queries showing tokenizations (baseline vs mirage) and top3 candidates?
anya: yes adding tokenization diff CSV and 50 failure cases (query, baseline-gt-rank, mirage-gt-rank, tokenization-before/after).
maya: also run ablation: move final LN back to pre-projection (we saw this often affects norm) and revert any pooling tweak. if tokenization is main culprit we should fix tokenizer, but if LN/pool also contributes we need ablation numbers.
luca: add per-lang paired t-tests on pos-sim means (baseline vs mirage) and report p-values + effect sizes. that helps prioritize.
ci-bot: nightly-eval started: job mirage-v1-multilang-onboard-20260409-01. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/mirage-v1-multilang-onboard-20260409-01/logs
mlops-bot: note: index build for PCA-whiten increases build time ~+18% and index size ~+5%. flagging for Dedicated config docs.
ben: good catch. plan summary?
anya: plan: 1) per-channel int8 calib sweep (symmetric/asym, clip percentiles) 2) HNSW efSearch sweep (64/128/256) 3) tokenizer-backfill experiments across es/ja/zh small samples 4) ablations: LN-placement + pooling-back 5) produce id-flip matrix and tokenization-diff CSV + 50 example cases 6) per-lang stats and paired tests. kicking jobs now - ETA ~1h for first pass.
maya: if tokenization is root, we should prioritize swapping tokenizer back for mirrored builds and re-run training. if LN/pooling is root, model fix. good job catching the language skew.
anya: thanks all :thumbsup: will post interim tables when jobs finish. closing until then.
